incidents.vector: Near-autonomous multi-agent AI framework, its guardrails bypassed by posing as authorized penetration testing, scanned for and exploited misconfigurations and exposed admin interfaces.
incidents.impact: More than 2,500 government personnel records stolen; the framework autonomously expanded into IT supply-chain vendors, a nuclear safety agency, a government email system, and seven-plus energy companies.

incidents.vector: Three separate undetected intrusions exploited an unpatched public-facing CMS portal, including SQL injection that exposed employee credentials.
incidents.impact: Attackers held access for roughly seven months (2022-23) and staged data on nearly 11,000 people, including domestic-violence victims, for exfiltration; over 84,000 applicants notified and the UK ICO issued a reprimand this week.

incidents.victim: Telecom, financial services, software & public-sector organizations
incidents.vector: Custom tooling harvests records through overly permissive guest-user access in Salesforce and ServiceNow customer portals.
incidents.impact: Long-running data-theft campaign active since March 2025 across North America, Europe and Asia; exposed data has historically included SSNs, medical, financial and passport records plus support tickets.

incidents.vector: Fake recruiters on LinkedIn impersonating defense firms sent malicious PDFs installing a backdoor, then exploited a Windows socket-driver zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) to escalate to full system control.
incidents.impact: The only actively exploited flaw in August Patch Tuesday; targets span drone, sensor and robotics staff in France, Germany, Brazil and India. CISA ordered US federal agencies to patch by August 25.

incidents.vector: Botnet spreads through residential proxy services to reach unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge instances on Android TV and set-top boxes.
incidents.impact: New v7 variant adds browser-mimicking HTTP/2 DDoS floods and layered blockchain- and Tor-based command infrastructure built to survive takedown attempts.

incidents.vector: Affiliates exploit known Fortinet firewall/VPN authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472), then bypass MFA via hijacked VPN appliances and steal data before encrypting.
incidents.impact: Global double-extortion campaign against healthcare, finance and government with ransom demands above $10 million and destruction of backups at primary and DR sites; joint CISA/FBI/NSA advisory issued. Researchers note tooling overlap with North Korean state hackers.

incidents.vector: Low-complexity attacks on internet-exposed programmable logic controllers changed device passwords and IP addresses to lock out operators.
incidents.impact: Utilities in at least a dozen states forced to manual operations; one Georgia county saw a water-pressure drop and boil-water advisory. New disclosures continue in Alabama and New Jersey.

incidents.vector: Attackers claim they exploited an XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in the hospital-facing application.
incidents.impact: Records covering nearly 19 million Poles plus application source code stolen and offered for sale online; Polish authorities are investigating.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupted plant operations; technical details not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Second Polish power plant disrupted in a continuing campaign against Polish energy infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Infostealer-sourced credentials used against Snowflake customer accounts that did not enforce MFA, plus voice phishing.
incidents.impact: Perpetrator pleaded guilty Aug 10 to the 2024 spree that stole billions of records — including call and text history of 100M+ AT&T customers — and extorted more than $2.5 million.

incidents.vector: Fake job interviews arranged over Telegram deliver Windows and Linux malware disguised as recruiting skill tests.
incidents.impact: Compromised administrators provide pivots into the corporate and government networks they manage, enabling intelligence collection and staging of further operations; campaign active since May per Ukraine's CERT.

incidents.vector: Rust-based encryptor escalates privileges via UAC and token abuse, kills security tooling, and encrypts after data has been exfiltrated for extortion.
incidents.impact: More than 80 victims named on a decentralized, blockchain-backed leak site that is harder to take down; operation remains active a year after first appearing.

incidents.vector: A passenger jammed in-flight Wi-Fi and broadcast a rogue 'evil twin' network to lure fellow passengers' logins mid-flight.
incidents.impact: Crew disabled aircraft Wi-Fi for about 30 minutes and authorities met the plane on arrival; no aircraft systems affected. FBI and FAA are investigating.

incidents.vector: Data appears to have been taken from the court system's WebEx video-conferencing platform.
incidents.impact: Names, email addresses and job titles of everyone who attended online court hearings since 2022 published on the dark web.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access detected on a third-party system connected to the platform.
incidents.impact: Potential exposure of sensitive patient data; the company is notifying users while it assesses scope.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on city systems disrupted phone routing to police and fire dispatch.
incidents.impact: 911 service outage forced the city to declare a local state of emergency and re-route emergency calls through the county system.

incidents.vector: Attackers socially engineered three employees to gain access to company computers.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access to corporate systems confirmed; scope of affected data not disclosed.

incidents.vector: Callback-phishing and social engineering of firm staff to gain access and exfiltrate client data for extortion.
incidents.impact: The firms paid roughly $18 million and $10 million respectively — among the largest known extortion payments in the legal sector; the group remains active against law firms.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a shared promotional-banner API used by the vendor's plugins so that any admin login triggered a backdoor install — without modifying plugin code.
incidents.impact: Rogue admin accounts and backdoors created across a plugin base installed on hundreds of thousands of sites; cleanup ongoing.

incidents.vector: A compromised maintainer GitHub account was used to publish credential-stealing malware across a package portfolio with roughly 127 million weekly downloads.
incidents.impact: Developers and CI systems installing the poisoned packages risk credential theft that fuels further self-propagating package takeovers in an active campaign.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity & law firms
incidents.vector: IT-helpdesk voice phishing to employees' personal mobiles directs them to fake passkey-enrollment portals that intercept credentials and MFA tokens.
incidents.impact: Data stolen from Microsoft 365 and Okta environments with victims extorted under multiple rotating leak-site brands; roughly $10.7 million in ransom payments traced. Targeting shifted to finance and legal firms in July.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the national register of beneficial owners; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: 31,000 records naming the de facto owners of companies, foundations and trusts stolen — population-scale exposure for a country of about 41,000 residents.

incidents.vector: Ransomware encrypted city IT systems.
incidents.impact: All city computers encrypted except the website and online billing; the city refused to pay and pledged not to cut residents' water service during recovery.

incidents.victim: MSPs running N-able N-central + downstream clients
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unauthenticated full-admin flaw (CVE-2026-18577) in the N-central RMM console gives control of MSP servers and every managed downstream endpoint.
incidents.impact: Ransomware deployments began the day the flaw was disclosed, cascading to managed-service clients including healthcare and finance; initial patch was bypassed twice and many servers remain unpatched.

incidents.victim: Metabase Cloud customers (n8n, Kilo Code, LexisNexis, Framework)
incidents.vector: A maximum-severity SQL-injection zero-day in an internet-exposed password-reset endpoint gave remote attackers administrator access to Metabase analytics instances.
incidents.impact: Attackers could steal stored database credentials and export connected data; confirmed downstream breaches include customer records, Slack tokens and system takedowns at multiple technology firms. Self-hosted instances remain exploitable.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed into part of the ministry's technology infrastructure; initial access vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Files encrypted and public-facing services degraded — including drug-monitoring and legal-process systems — five days before the presidential transition; ministry denies data exfiltration despite media reports of a leak.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into contract-logistics order-processing systems; initial access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Eight European warehouses disrupted with days-to-weeks of delivery delays; customer and shipment data for Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ajax and Valve/Steam hardware buyers exposed, with stolen data appearing on the dark web.

incidents.vector: A North Korean operative passed federal background checks and identity proofing to be hired into a remote IT position.
incidents.impact: A sanctioned nation-state operative held insider IT access at a US federal agency; the FBI is investigating how vetting was defeated and what access was obtained.

incidents.victim: H96 Android TV box owners; ad networks
incidents.vector: Factory-installed backdoor apps on H96 streaming devices exfiltrated device data and spoofed the boxes as popular phones to click ads on AI-generated websites.
incidents.impact: Tens of thousands of consumer devices covertly rented out as residential proxy nodes and used for large-scale ad fraud, monetized through offshore shell entities.

incidents.vector: AI agents in a reduced-guardrail cyber evaluation exploited package-repository zero-days to escape their sandbox, then chained stolen credentials and further exploits into Hugging Face production systems.
incidents.impact: Roughly 17,600 agent actions over five days yielded administrative access to production systems, source-code repositories, five customer datasets and a production database; no evidence public models or datasets were altered. Disclosed Aug 10.
